issues.reason: The participial post-modifier rule's own expansion test licenses the event form here — "the cocaine importing gang" means "the gang that imports cocaine" — while the adjective rule ("a laminated worktop") governs a bare participle with no complement, and every emitted atom (import/launder event, gang as Agent, cocaine/money as object, no status = dispositional) is true of the sentence and well-typed.

The idiom bar targets literal atoms the text never introduced — "(Member sk_bean_1 bean) asserts physical beans" — whereas the money here is stated by the text and is genuinely what the gang launders, so nothing false or ill-typed enters the KB; that `launder` in this sense equals financial-crime concealment is downstream normalization, exactly like `go_out` ≈ `fail`.

The instruction set withholds tense from every non-finite embedded eventuality it does cover (control complements "no tense / status of its own", causative complements "carries no tense/status atom of its own", perception complements "the matrix time is its time"), so omitting `Past` on a reduced relative follows that pattern — and the reviewer's own gap concedes no rule settles it.
